title: The Double Ghost
premise: Lena Coldharbour, a veteran crash investigator, has spent two decades chasing the truth about the 'accident' that killed her family in row twelve — a crash she was told to stop investigating. When a safe house used by the conspiracy's fixers is listed online with interior photos, Lena and her ragtag team of exiled investigators spot evidence of a staged attack being planned: a passenger jet downed to look like mechanical failure. Racing a deadline set by men who rewrite rules for a living, they must expose the plot before it flies — and before the mole inside their own found family betrays them. In the end, Lena chooses justice over vengeance, forcing a public reckoning at the cost of her career, and finally buries row twelve.
about_author: Freya Ashgrove is a former aviation safety analyst who left the industry after a case she was ordered to close refused to stay closed. She writes thrillers from a coastal cottage, where she keeps a wall of unsolved incident reports as research — and as a promise.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Twenty years after the crash, Lena walks the reconstructed fuselage of Flight 4471 in a training hangar, touching seat markers while reciting the official findings she never believed. A call from her old mentor warns her someone is asking questions again. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into discipline; the wound reopened on page one.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: POV: Dev, Lena's protégé and hacker. While scraping property records, Dev finds a rural safe house listed for sale — with photos showing documents, maps, and a whiteboard referencing an upcoming 'delivery.' He recognizes the handwriting style from the 4471 file. Emotional beat: electric discovery, the past surfacing in the most mundane place imaginable.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Getting Rewritten
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She presents the listing to her small circle of exiled investigators — Mara, a disgraced NTSB analyst; Okafor, a fired air marshal; and Dev. They map what's visible in the photos against old case files and find overlapping names. Emotional beat: cautious hope; a family of the discarded reassembling around one clue.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Posing as a cash buyer, Okafor tours the safe house and confirms the whiteboard was scrubbed but not cleaned — ghost impressions remain under raking light. He photographs everything, then realizes he's being followed off the property. Emotional beat: dread blooming beneath competence; the hunt has noticed them back.

chapters.title: Ghost Impressions
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Back at their cramped office, Mara reconstructs the whiteboard from shadow lines: a date six weeks out, an aircraft registration, and the word 'ROW TWELVE.' Lena goes silent when she sees it. Emotional beat: vertigo — the conspiracy isn't repeating history by accident; it's quoting it.

chapters.title: The Registration
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The tail number traces to a shell company layered through three jurisdictions, ultimately tied to Meridian Aviation Services — the same maintenance contractor certified the original 4471 aircraft airworthy. Emotional beat: cold fury; twenty years of 'coincidence' collapsing into design.

chapters.title: What the Widow Knew
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena tracks down Ilse Brandt, widow of the 4471 first officer, who reveals her husband mailed her a letter the day before the crash — a letter she was pressured to surrender and never read. Emotional beat: tenderness and rage entwined; another family broken by the same machine.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV (interleaved with Lena). The recovered letter describes a 'modification' installed days before departure and names a supervisor at Meridian. Ilse gives Lena a copy she hid inside a child's book for twenty years. Emotional beat: inheritance of courage; proof passed hand to hand like contraband.

chapters.title: Countermove
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Within hours of the letter surfacing, their office lease is terminated, Mara's bank accounts freeze, and a federal 'inquiry' into Lena's credentials opens. Someone inside is feeding them intel — or feeding them out. Emotional beat: siege pressure; the system closing like a fist.

chapters.title: The Mole Question
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The team fractures over suspicion: only four people knew about the letter, and the retaliation came within hours. Dev defends his source; Okafor points at Mara's frozen accounts as too convenient. Emotional beat: trust cracking; found family tested by the enemy's oldest trick.

chapters.title: Delivery Date
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Decoding flight-plan chatter bought from a sympathetic dispatcher, Dev pins the staged attack: a charter flight, six weeks out, carrying a whistleblower scheduled to testify against Meridian. The crash will kill the testimony. Emotional beat: the clock starts audibly ticking; stakes become human and specific.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Against everyone's advice, Lena contacts the whistleblower, Ansel Voss, through a burner channel. Voss is terrified, half-convinced they're part of the trap. Lena offers him the one thing no one offered her family: the truth in advance. Emotional beat: fragile alliance; duty and love pulling in opposite directions.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The team moves Voss to a borrowed cabin. That night, drones sweep the treeline — surveillance, not yet attack. Okafor realizes the enemy wants them gathered in one place. Emotional beat: claustrophobia; safety revealed as bait.

chapters.title: Confession at the Cabin
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Cornered by conscience, Voss admits he once signed off on falsified inspection reports for 4471 — he was the pen, not the hand. Lena, hearing the man who papered over her family's death beg to make it right, must choose between hatred and use. Emotional beat: the book's moral hinge; forgiveness as strategy, not absolution.

chapters.title: The Hand Behind the Pen
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Following Voss's memory of signatures, Mara identifies Aldous Rehm — now a regulator overseeing the very investigation that cleared Meridian. Rehm authored every rewritten rule Lena ever choked on. Emotional beat: the architecture of corruption made visible; the villain gets a face.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. The mole is exposed: not a teammate but Dev's trusted dispatcher contact, who sold their location to Rehm's fixers. A strike team hits the cabin at dawn; Okafor holds the treeline while the others scatter. Voss is taken. Emotional beat: violent rupture; the cost of trust paid in blood and absence.

chapters.title: Scattered
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Regrouping in a motel outside the city, the survivors count losses: Voss captive, Okafor wounded, evidence half-burned. Lena proposes the unthinkable — go public with everything, unverified, before the flight. Mara argues they'll be discredited forever. Emotional beat: despair transmuting into resolve; imperfect justice versus perfect silence.

chapters.title: Two Days Out
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Using old marshal channels, Okafor learns the charter's route and a fuel stop where Rehm's people will stage the 'mechanical' failure. The team splits: Mara and Dev build the evidentiary package for press and prosecutors; Lena and Okafor go physical. Emotional beat: converging momentum; every thread pulled taut.

chapters.title: The Fuel Stop
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. At a rain-slicked regional airstrip, Lena photographs technicians installing a sabotaged component, matching the modification described in the dead first officer's letter — twenty years apart, identical hands. Rehm himself appears to supervise. Emotional beat: the past and present colliding in one frame; vindication and terror in the same breath.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, climax. Confronting Rehm on the apron with recording running, Lena forces him to speak the plan aloud as federal agents — tipped by Mara's simultaneous document drop — close in. Rehm orders the hit anyway; Okafor disables the sabotage crew; the flight is grounded mid-taxi. Emotional beat: catharsis without triumph; justice arriving battered and just in time.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Voss, rescued in the raid's aftermath, testifies; Meridian collapses; hearings reopen 4471 with the letter entered into record. Lena watches from the gallery, unnamed, as officials read her family's names correctly for the first time. Emotional beat: quiet devastation and release; the record corrected, though nothing restored.

chapters.title: After the Findings
chapters.summary: Lena's POV, resolution. Lena declines a reinstatement offer and instead founds an independent accident-review collective with Mara, Dev, and Okafor — rules written by people who can't rewrite them. She visits the graves in row twelve's order and, for the first time, leaves before dark. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given; love outlasting duty's wreckage.
